shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for store.opened 100; record.committed 200 (replayed) and 201; record.invalid 400; record.conflict 409; record.stale 412; store.corrupt 500; store.wal_large 500; store.busy 503; store.disk 503; store.unavailable 503; stream.slow 503. Owner-acts: store.corrupt, store.unavailable, store.disk after N-45 ran.
records(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, id UNIQUE, at, code, kind, node, ticket, attempt, body JSON, hash); append-only; seq strictly increasing.
entities(key PRIMARY KEY, kind, version, body JSON, updated_seq, updated_at); version grows by one per write; updated_seq is the seq of the record that last wrote it.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.
The forward-only migration table and the rule that the node owning a table owns its migration.
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; canonical JSON by RFC 8785 for the hash.
Compare-and-swap: expected_version on an entity write; 409 with the current version on a miss; expected 0 inserts.
One store, no broker, SQLite under the state root, never in the repository (D10 C34, D04 C35).
Many agents at once from the first line: atomic writes, append-only records, leases with fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report.
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
Every Put a seat makes carries the lease token its launcher exported; the seat never sees another seat's token; a stale token is 412 and is logged.
The ctl verbs a seat may call: record add (seat.result, heartbeat, note), record get, record list, ticket get, health; never the file or the socket directly.
quick_check not ok at open: NOT_SERVING, a prepared dry-run restore from the newest verified backup, one card; never an automatic restore over the live file.
Free space under store.min_free_mib: Puts refused 503 store.disk, N-45 cleanup first, then one card.

purpose.is: N-01 is the one durable store of the factory: every record any node writes, every entity any node claims or versions, lives in one SQLite file on the WSL host, owned by the Go service, reachable only through one gRPC socket.
It is the carrier of every edge in the DAG: an output record of any node is a Put here, and the sequence number it returns is what the push transport (N-31) fans out.
purpose.is-not: It is not a broker, a bus, a queue daemon or a second copy of anything: no broker (D10, C34), no records branch, no records tree in the repository (D04, C35, memory rule runtime-data-never-in-the-repo).
It does not decide anything: no routing, no retry policy, no verdict lives here; those are N-07, N-11 and the gate nodes.
purpose.decisions: D01 (Go service with gRPC owns state), D10 (one store, SQLite on the host, backups scheduled), D04 (tickets and all artifacts in the state root), D22 (the Go service on the WSL host).

record.who: Any node of the Go service in-process, the ctl CLI run by the same user, a seat through the ctl CLI with its lease token, the push transport for acks.
record.field: Caller-chosen string, unique per intended effect: node id, colon, the input record id, colon, the step name. A second Put with the same key returns the first commit unchanged.
The record body: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, and the kind's own fields, valid against the kind's schema under its node directory.
An optional entity write in the same transaction: key, expected_version, body. Absent means append-only, no compare-and-swap.
Required when the caller holds a lease (N-02): the fencing token the lease granted. The store refuses a stale token (412).

input.rule: A Put is one transaction: the record row, the entity row and the idempotency row commit together or not at all.

record.field: Monotonic store sequence, assigned at commit, never reused, the cursor of N-31 and of every List.
The record id as the caller wrote it, form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-CODE-xxxxx (events/schema/event.schema.json#id).
sha256 of the canonical JSON body, so a replay can be compared byte for byte.
The entity version after the write, when an entity was written; absent otherwise.
true when the idempotency key was already committed and this answer is the stored one (code 200, not 201).
The entity key whose expected_version did not match.
What the store holds, so the caller re-reads and decides.

output.rule: A 409 is itself appended to the log as a record (kind record.conflict) so a collision is visible, never silent.
A Put that fails validation is 400 record.invalid with the failing path; nothing is written except the 400 record.

mechanism.component: One SQLite database at the state root: STATE/store/coq.db with its -wal and -shm files. PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=FULL, busy_timeout=5000, foreign_keys=ON, wal_autocheckpoint=1000. Source: S03 section 8 item 6.

Go package scheduler/internal/store in the small cut (D09, C41): Open, Put, Get, List, Tail, Snapshot, Close. Pure functions for canonical JSON and hashing; the clock is the core.Clock interface so tests set it (scheduler/internal/core/interfaces.go#Clock).

gRPC service coq.store.v1.Store on a unix socket XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/coq/store.sock, mode 0600, no TCP, same user only. RPCs: Put, Get, List, Tail (server stream to N-31 and the ctl CLI), Snapshot (N-05), Health (grpc.health.v1).
One writer goroutine owns every write transaction; callers queue on a bounded channel (store.put_queue 256). Readers use a pool of read connections; WAL lets them read while the writer writes.
mechanism.tables: The table definitions live in the shared state-store volume, declared below as needs (shared need: shared/state-store.xml, anchors table-records, table-entities, table-idempotency); this node owns those three tables and their migrations. records(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, id UNIQUE, at, code, kind, node, ticket, attempt, body JSON, hash); append-only. entities(key PRIMARY KEY, kind, version, body JSON, updated_seq, updated_at); compare-and-swap on version. idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response. Other G1 nodes own leases (N-02), claims and tickets (N-03), forge (N-04), backups (N-05), ticks and health (N-06) rows in the same file; each declares its own table need in its own volume.
mechanism.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant C as caller (node, ctl, seat with token) participant S as Store gRPC participant W as writer goroutine participant DB as coq.db (WAL) C->>S: Put(idempotency_key, record, entity?, lease_token?) S->>S: validate body against kind schema S->>W: enqueue (bounded, 5 s) W->>DB: BEGIN IMMEDIATE W->>DB: SELECT seq FROM idempotency WHERE key=? alt key seen W-->>C: 200 record.committed replayed=true else new W->>DB: check lease token current (412 if stale) W->>DB: UPDATE entities SET version=version+1 WHERE key=? AND version=expected (409 if 0 rows) W->>DB: INSERT records (seq assigned) W->>DB: INSERT idempotency (key, seq, response) W->>DB: COMMIT W-->>C: 201 record.committed (seq, hash, version) W->>S: notify Tail streams (seq) end
mechanism.step: Validate: envelope fields present, at is UTC form, code is in the shared map, kind has a schema; else 400.
Idempotency: a committed key returns its stored response with code 200 and replayed true; the log gets no new row.
Fencing: when lease_token is present, the leases table must hold that token for the record's ticket and attempt; else 412 record.stale, and the 412 is logged with the token seen.
Compare-and-swap: when entity is present, UPDATE ... WHERE key AND version = expected; zero rows means 409 with the current version; a missing key with expected 0 is an insert.
Append: INSERT the record; seq is the rowid of the records table, strictly increasing; hash computed over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces).
Commit with synchronous FULL, then notify Tail streams with the new seq; a stream that is not reading within 1 s is dropped and must reconnect with a full re-read (D21).
mechanism.canonical: Canonical JSON: RFC 8785 ordering, UTF-8, no insignificant whitespace; the same function serves the hash, the backup checksum (N-05) and the replay comparison.
mechanism.ids: Record id as today: UTC stamp, code, five-character suffix (events/schema/event.schema.json#id). The id is unique per writer; the store refuses a duplicate id with 409 record.conflict key=id.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. The systemd user unit of N-06 starts the binary; the store is opened in the binary's start sequence before any tick, and READY=1 is not sent to systemd until the store answers Health SERVING.
start.step: Resolve the state root with bin/state-root.sh (COQ_STATE, else XDG state home, coq, repo name). A relative root is exit 3 and the unit fails loudly.
Create STATE/store/ 0700 when absent; open coq.db; apply the schema migration table (shared need: shared/state-store.xml, anchor migrations) forward only.
Run PRAGMA quick_check with a 60 s bound. ok starts the service; anything else goes to the recovery path in retries.
Replay is automatic: WAL frames since the last checkpoint are applied by SQLite on open. The store records store.opened 100 with the top seq and the file size.
Expose the socket; answer Health SERVING; N-06 then starts the ticks.

wait.name: busy
wait.fallback: 503 store.busy to the caller; the caller retries per retries; no row is written

wait.name: put-queue
wait.fallback: 503 store.busy; counter store.queue_full increments; health degrades at 3 in one minute

wait.name: quick-check
wait.fallback: treated as a failed open; recovery path

wait.name: checkpoint
wait.timeout: every 1000 pages or 60 s, whichever first; PASSIVE, TRUNCATE at drain
wait.fallback: a checkpoint that cannot complete 3 times in a row records store.wal_large 500 at 256 MiB

wait.name: tail-send
wait.fallback: the stream is closed with code 503 stream.slow; the client reconnects and re-reads from its last seq

wait.name: disk
wait.fallback: below store.min_free_mib 512 the store refuses Puts with 503 store.disk and health goes unhealthy

wait.name: drain
wait.fallback: the process exits anyway; SQLite rolls back the open transaction on next open

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports (principles no-cog, three-attempts).
retries.step: A 503 from the store is retried by the caller 3 times with 1, 2, 4 s backoff and the same idempotency key, so a retry can never double-write; the fourth failure is the caller's own failure record with reason store.

Open failing (lock, io, schema) is retried 3 times 5 s apart; then the unit stays up, Health answers NOT_SERVING, store.unavailable 503 goes to the N-06 health record and the journal, and N-28 raises one card from the owner-acts code. The unit does not crash-loop on a bad file.

quick_check not ok: 3 attempts of PRAGMA integrity_check then VACUUM INTO a fresh file; still not ok means restore from the newest verified backup (N-05 runbook restore) is prepared as a dry-run listing, store.corrupt 500 is reported, and the owner's card carries the restore command. The store never restores over the live file on its own, because the newest records since the backup would be lost silently.

A 409 is never retried blindly by the store; the caller re-reads the entity and decides. A node that retries a 409 does so at most 3 times with a fresh read each time, then writes its own failure record.

many-agents.reading: Twenty seats and every node read this volume and the store at once: reads are WAL snapshot reads on a pool of connections, never blocked by the writer; List and Get are pure reads keyed by seq or id, so N readers see one consistent version each.
many-agents.working: No agent touches coq.db. A seat writes only through the ctl CLI on the socket, with the lease token its run was given; a pod never reaches the host socket and reports through GitHub statuses (N-25) that N-04 reads.
many-agents.collision: Two callers Put the same idempotency key: the writer serializes them; the first commits 201, the second gets the stored response with code 200 replayed true. No double row.

Two callers write one entity with the same expected_version: the first commits and bumps the version; the second gets 409 with the current version and a logged record.conflict; it re-reads and re-decides.

A seat whose lease expired and was re-granted to a fresh attempt still tries to write: its token is no longer current and the Put is 412 record.stale, logged, so the old run cannot overwrite the new one (fencing, T06).
Two writers mint the same record id in the same second: the UNIQUE index on id refuses the second with 409 key=id; the writer re-mints the suffix and retries, up to 3 times.
A reader holds a snapshot while a checkpoint runs: SQLite WAL guarantees the reader's view; the checkpoint is PASSIVE and simply does less work.
many-agents.test: Two processes (the service and the ctl CLI) and two goroutines Put 1000 records each with overlapping keys and entities; the proof is: exactly one row per key, every 409 logged, seq strictly increasing with no gap, hash recomputed equals stored.

nobody for the old holder; N-12 already handled the stall; the record is evidence
owner, through one card from N-28 that carries the prepared restore

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor; a code missing there fails check.sh.

path.cleanup: removed at drain; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes a stale one when no pid holds it

path.writer: N-01 structured log, one line per Put over 100 ms and per non-2xx

state-paths.rule: STATE is the state root from bin/state-root.sh; nothing under it is ever committed. Every cleanup script defaults to dry-run and prints what it would delete; --apply deletes; both exit 0 on nothing to do, 3 when the unit is running and the path is live.
cleanup-store.sh refuses --apply unless the unit is stopped and N-05 lists a verified backup newer than the newest seq; it prints the backup path it checked.

edges.in: every output of every node is a Put; the return writes are not drawn

out.record: record.committed on ticket.ready and lease rows

Put with a seen key returns 200 replayed=true and adds no row.
Entity write with a wrong expected_version returns 409 and logs record.conflict.

item.check: Put with a stale lease token returns 412.
item.proof: Go test with a lease re-granted to attempt 2.

item.check: Two processes writing concurrently leave seq gapless and strictly increasing.
Tail delivers every committed seq in order; a slow client is dropped with 503 and re-reads.
item.proof: Go test with a blocked stream.

item.check: quick_check runs at open within 60 s and a corrupt file leads to NOT_SERVING, not a crash loop.
item.proof: Test with a truncated file; journal shows one store.corrupt and the unit active.

item.check: No path under the repository is written.
item.proof: `git status --porcelain` empty after the full test run, saved in the test log.

item.check: Every state path above has its cleanup script, dry-run by default.

actor.name: Go service (N-01 to N-12, N-28 to N-31, N-43 to N-51)
actor.may: Put, Get, List, Tail, Snapshot in-process

actor.name: ctl CLI, same user
actor.may: Put, Get, List, Tail over the socket; Put of kinds the shared seat contract allows a seat (seat.result, heartbeat, note) only with a current lease token

actor.name: seat (one-shot run)
actor.may: only the ctl CLI verbs its rendered settings allow (N-13); never the file, never the socket directly

actor.name: pod
actor.may: nothing here; reports through GitHub statuses

actor.name: owner
actor.may: everything, through the ctl CLI and the break-glass path; a direct sqlite3 session on the live file is break glass and is recorded by the runbook step

permissions.rule: The socket is mode 0600 under the owner's user; there is no TCP listener (scheduler/api/scheduler/v1/scheduler.proto header, h-proto-sockets).

counter.name: store.put_latency_ms
counter.alarm: p99 over 500 ms for 3 health ticks

check.name: store.health
check.ok: a SELECT 1 under 100 ms and free space above the floor
check.else: 503 store.unavailable or store.disk, latched: one record per transition

monitoring.surface: Counters appear in the Status answer (N-06), on the Stats screen (N-40) and as a machine panel (N-39) bound to the health entity; alerts reach the Alerts screen (N-41) through their codes.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl store status` prints top seq, db and wal bytes, tail clients, last checkpoint. Read-only.
`scheduler ctl record get ID` or `scheduler ctl record list --since SEQ --kind KIND`.
`scheduler ctl store checkpoint` (PASSIVE); only when store.wal_large fired; it is a break-glass-free action because it changes no data.

Stop the unit (`systemctl --user stop coq-service`), run `scheduler/host/bin/restore-store.sh --from BACKUP --dry-run`, read the listing, then `--apply`; it moves the live file aside with a UTC stamp, copies the backup, runs integrity_check, and starts the unit. The newest records after the backup are lost and the script prints the seq gap; that gap is the card's content.
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-store.sh, cleanup-run.sh, cleanup-logs.sh as listed in state-paths; dry-run first, always.
A direct `sqlite3 STATE/store/coq.db` write session is owner-only, one time, recorded as break.glass before and after, with the unit stopped.

item.what: NATS JetStream as the store or wake bus
item.reason: C34 ruled no broker; the failure class was addressing, which a broker stores but does not fix (S03 F3)

item.what: one file per record and one file per job in the state root as the store
item.reason: a directory of files has no compare-and-swap, no sequence and no single-writer guarantee; the one-file-per-record log is kept as the record id form and the append-only principle (V01), the files are not

item.what: the scheduler never writes a record file itself; the executor runs events/bin/event.sh
item.reason: the store is the writer now; event.sh's validation (schema, code enum, exclusive create) moves into Put; event.sh becomes the ctl CLI's `record add` verb so the single-writer rule survives

item.what: no streaming call on the control plane (h-proto-stream)
item.reason: D21 (C52) rules push for everything; Tail is the one server stream, limited to seq fan-out, with full re-read on reconnect; the no-stream rule stays for every other RPC

item.what: the repository copy of the record log (S2) and the three stranded roots (S11)
item.reason: two sources of truth (K07); N-49 reconciles them into this store once, then deletes

item.what: PostgreSQL or Redis behind the service
item.reason: a second daemon on a host with eleven bugchecks; SQLite needs none and survives a process kill (S03 section 8 item 6)

item.what: the Drive control_plane.proto WorkOrderService as the store API
item.reason: its lease, version and receipt shapes are carried (N-02, this Put's expected_version); its fifteen WorkState values and four services are more than the small cut needs (D09)
